title: Content Management and Publishing
priorKnowledge: Understand schemas, versions, workflows, cache, and search.
owner: Owning content/catalog module, workflow, nPublish, version providers, and target adapter
summary: Business users edit versioned staged records, approval workflows authorize a version, and nPublish deploys that approved form to a separate online authority.

sections.heading: End-to-end example
items: Business user creates or updates content in Staged.
The change set is associated with a workflow carrier.
Manual and automatic validation, enrichment, and approval actions execute.
Final approval requests publication of the exact approved version.
nPublish validates dependencies and calls the domain adapter.
The adapter deploys through authenticated target transport to Online; it does not write the Online database directly.
Online cache invalidates or refreshes and search reconciles through their existing contracts.
Storefront serves only the published online form.

sections.heading: Two runtime authorities
items: Staged activates configured version variants and keeps editable immutable versions.
Online does not activate version variants and stores the deployed target form.
Versioning is enabled per module/schema; a user schema need not be versioned while content or catalog schemas may be.
nPublish is the single provider-neutral publication lifecycle; domains contribute adapters and dependency rules, not parallel state machines.
